recipes.name: Southern Green Beans
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds fresh green beans, trimmed and snapped

steps.text: Cook chopped bacon in a skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until evenly browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain bacon pieces on a paper towel-lined plate.
Melt butter in a skillet with a lid over medium-low heat. Add onion; cook and stir until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in cooked bacon, green beans, potatoes, garlic, and chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer over low heat until green beans are tender, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with vinegar, salt, and pepper; serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: These Southern green beans cooked with potatoes get great flavor from onion sautéed in butter, crisp bacon, and a splash of white balsamic vinegar.

video.description: Want delicious potatoes, green beans, and bacon all in one amazing side dish? Well this is it! It’s flavorful, full of garlic, bacon, and will compliment any main dish. Buttery and delightful for family and guests alike.

review.reviewBody: One of my friends described this as 'German Potato Salad' meets Green Beans which is a great combo!! Here's my suggestions for next time: -- substitute red potatoes if you don't have new potatoes and dice them into 1/2 inch chunks -- after cooking the bacon, remove it and cook the onions in the bacon fat. Add another T or 2 of butter if necessary -- once the onion is cooked, add the potatoes and garlic. Cook for a couple minutes and then add the green beans and broth -- do not add too much broth as this will make your 'sauce' too soupy. -- make sure you have a large enough pot to be able to mix the vegetables as they cook. Otherwise the bottom cooks and the top is still raw. -- Once the dish is plated, sprinkle the bacon on top for an attractive presentation. -- Enjoy!!
Southern green beans don't crunch when you bite into them. These need to be cooked in a slow cooker for 4-6 hours to be real southern green beans.

We have never liked the traditional green bean casserole with mushroom soup. I decided to give this a try this year, and it is delicious! I did tweak it a bit. I cooked the onions and green beans in the bacon fat, then tossed in the potatoes to soak up the rest. Then I added the garlic and chicken broth. I doubled the amount of potatoes just to bulk it up for our big crowd. Drizzled it with an orange balsamic vinegar just before serving. It was a huge crowd pleaser!

I am not sure where in the South this is from. Maybe Northern Virginia? These were tasty but my people (all Southerners cook green beans with some butter and country ham chunks for 8 hours on low - beyond all nutritional value. :)
I made this following directions closely, except I used my Dutch oven and cooked them about 25 to 30 minutes so beans and potatoes were well-done. My family loved it!

Have made these several times - the first 3-4 times as written (except for the vinegar - can't do that!). They are quite good and close to those my Texas grandmother made 70 odd years ago. Since they are only "close" to what she made I have made some adjustments for my family in an attempt to make them more like hers. I put chopped UNCOOKED bacon, as well as the onion (very coarsely chopped) into the pot with the potatoes and the beans. I also omit the balsamic vinegar. My grandmother did not use chicken broth in her beans, but I do that - only I start with an entire can of broth and top up with water as needed. In the case of water in this dish, to me "less is more." I also cook longer than 10 minutes, maybe about 30 minutes, so that the beans are quite soft and the bacon is soft enough to be pleasing in a bite. This is a go-to company dish when I want to concentrate on my meat. It is easy enough to leave me plenty of time for whatever else I'm preparing. Thank you for posting this and reminding me of Grandmother's beans.

Good flavor. I added the vinegar during the cooking process and added a tablespoon of brown sugar to counter the vinegar flavor. I added a little extra broth because I didn't "dice" the potatoes small enough so it took about twice as long to cook. Also, consider adding the fresh green beans a little after you've let the potatoes get somewhat soft so you don't overcook the beans. Overall ... very good.

Last night I made this for my Georgia boring adult children. I loved it, even the DC born child. I took a shortcut by cooking the green beans in my instant pot for 5 minutes the day before. This part of my family likes their green beans really well cooked so the pre-cooking solved that problem.

We love the flavors but there is no way the potatoes are cooked by the time the beans are cooked. So I now put the potatoes into the pan and cook them until they are nearly done then add the beans. I made it again today and it was delicious.
Delicious! I took the bacon out, kept the grease, and cooked everything in the pan with it… I’m never making green beans any other way, thanks for the recipe!

Great taste! I added more chicken broth to allow the green beans to steam/simmer a little longer so they were not quite so crunchy. Added more balsamic vinegar at the end, dark vinegar as I did not have white. And more bacon is ALWAYS perfect. Family loved it!

Being a southern gal I like my green beans very soft so I just cooked them longer. I added white vinegar instead of balsamic and added half ham in place of half the bacon since I ran out. It was absolutely delicious!

I prepared this as set out. The flavour profile was excellent. Everything was perfect except the bacon. Maybe I missed something, but adding cooked bacon at the same time as broth seems to be poor timing. It became soggy and flavorless. Maybe it should have been added towards the end. I will try it this way next time. A recipe worth refining for sure.
Made pretty much as written. I did the onions and garlic in bacon grease. I cooked mine in a crock pot for three hours on high. Came out great.
These green beans are now a permanent side dish to complement our Christmas Eve standing rib roast dinner🤩
I hate soft and mushy green beans. I cooked onion and potatoes in broth till they were half way cooked. Added beans and cooked for 10 minutes. Perfectly cooked green beans and potatoes were done.
Yummy! I love it! Couldn’t have the bacon so I added vegetable oil.

If you cook fresh green beans, you have to cook longer than 10 minutes covered on simmer. I cooked mine an extra 10 minutes on medium heat covered and the were perfect. As far as the rest of the recipe, great. They tasted wonderful. One addition that worked for me thought it is not really healthy - don’t dispose of the bacon grease, just add the butter to it. Yummmmmm!
